claims.statement: From 18 February 2027, industrial batteries above 2 kWh, LMT batteries and EV batteries require an electronic battery passport and QR linkage.
The regulation permits authorised operators to store or process passport data but restricts reuse beyond the contracted service, supporting a trustee-shaped role.
Demand and economics hypothesis: smaller C&I battery suppliers will outsource passport infrastructure instead of building secure lifecycle data services internally.

contrary_evidence: Large OEMs and industry consortia are likely to build or standardise their own passport infrastructure.
The passport applies only to specified battery categories, narrowing the initial market.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: lab and distributor bundles reach many smaller Asian and Central-European suppliers entering the EU
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 75 OEMs and 250000 active batteries could produce 8-14m PLN ARR; a trusted EU data utility could put founder equity above 5m PLN in 4-7 years
economics.founder_time: 18-24 hours weekly for a narrow storage-battery pilot; security work outsourced
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 75-88% after standard connectors and automated validation
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 12-18 months with ten model integrations and 15000 active units
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 20000-60000 PLN per model integration plus 8-25 PLN per active battery annually
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every new model, serialised unit, ownership change, repair and end-of-life event

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal model-to-unit provenance, validated supplier connectors and lifecycle continuity make the trustee costly to replace
fingerprint.customer: EU battery OEMs and importers supplying commercial and industrial energy-storage systems
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded referrals and connectors through accredited test laboratories, BMS vendors and ESS distributors
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Managed data onboarding, identifier and permissioned passport hosting with usage-based fleet fees
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: OEM or importer pays per model onboarding, passport issuance and active fleet year
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered battery model is prepared for EU placement and needs a QR-linked passport with controlled, up-to-date evidence

founder_fit: Energy-storage adjacency to the family renewable business
Can validate on a few models before substantial capital deployment
risks: Security or availability failure would damage a trust-based position.
Standards and delegated acts may favour incumbent global platforms.
OEM source data may be incomplete or commercially sensitive.

structure.control_point: The signed passport release and QR identity required before covered batteries enter service
structure.critical_dependency: Final implementing specifications, secure source data and continued trust from economic operators

thesis: A neutral data trustee distributed by battery laboratories and commercial-storage distributors could ingest test, bill-of-materials and lifecycle evidence, issue persistent identifiers and host role-based battery passports for industrial batteries above 2 kWh. It would preserve provenance, not certify conformity. Demand and economics are hypotheses.
title: Battery-Passport Data Trustee for C&I Storage
uncertainties: Whether labs will endorse a neutral data provider
